title: Ravana seeks Mareecha's help
introduction: Ravana seeks Maareecha's help to abduct Seetha. He asks Maareecha to assume the shape of a golden-deer and lure Seetha, and then Seetha asks Rama and Lakshmana to fetch that golden-deer. If Rama and Lakshmana are distracted from the hermitage, Ravana can safely abduct Seetha. Listening to this Maareecha is struck dead, because he is already struck with the arrow of Rama when he was in Tataka forest. As such, Maareecha tries to explain Ravana about Rama's quintessence.
closing: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये अरण्य काण्डे षट् त्रिंशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 36th chapter in Aranya Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
मारीच श्रूयताम् तात वचनम् मम भाषतः |
आर्तो अस्मि मम च आर्तस्य भवान् हि परमा गतिः
verses.iast:
mārīca śrūyatām tāta vacanam mama bhāṣataḥ |
ārto asmi mama ca ārtasya bhavān hi paramā gatiḥ
verses.translation: "Give attention to my words as I speak, oh, sire, Maareecha, I am an anguished one, and when I am in such an anguish you are the ultimate course to me, isn't so." Thus Ravana started addressing Maareecha.

glosses.meaning: as I speak, my, sentence, listen - give attention
you are, ultimate, course, isn't it.

verses.devanagari:
जानीषे त्वम् जनस्थाने भ्राता यत्र खरो मम |
दूषणः च महाबाहुः स्वसा शूर्पणखा च मे
त्रिशिराः च महातेजा राक्षसः पिशित अशनः |
अन्ये च बहवः शूरा लब्ध लक्षा निशाचराः
वसन्ति मत् नियोगेन अधिवासम् च राक्षसः |
बाधमाना महारण्ये मुनीन् ये धर्म चारिणः
verses.iast:
jānīṣe tvam janasthāne bhrātā yatra kharo mama |
dūṣaṇaḥ ca mahābāhuḥ svasā śūrpaṇakhā ca me
triśirāḥ ca mahātejā rākṣasaḥ piśita aśanaḥ |
anye ca bahavaḥ śūrā labdha lakṣā niśācarāḥ
vasanti mat niyogena adhivāsam ca rākṣasaḥ |
bādhamānā mahāraṇye munīn ye dharma cāriṇaḥ
verses.translation: "You are aware as to how my brother Khara, and the mighty armed Duushana, also my sister Shuurpanakha, and even the highly fiery demon and devourer of raw-flesh Trishira, and even numerous other night-walking demons who are cocksure of hitting their targets have made Janasthaana as their residency, and while residing there they put the sages of that great forest that tread a righteous path to torture, of course, all this as assigned by me.

glosses.itrans: mahaatejaa pishita ashanaH raakSasaH trishiraaH ca
glosses.iast: mahātejā piśita aśanaḥ rākṣasaḥ triśirāḥ ca
glosses.devanagari: महातेजा पिशित अशनः राक्षसः त्रिशिराः च
glosses.meaning: highly fiery one, raw-flesh, devourer, demon, Trishira, also
those who obtained, target - those that can hit target without missing
righteousness, treaders in, sages, while torturing

verses.devanagari:
चतुर्दश सहस्राणि रक्षसाम् भीम कर्मणाम् |
शूराणाम् लब्ध लक्षाणाम् खर चित्त अनुवर्तिनाम्
ते तु इदानीम् जनस्थाने वसमाना महाबलाः |
verses.iast:
caturdaśa sahasrāṇi rakṣasām bhīma karmaṇām |
śūrāṇām labdha lakṣāṇām khara citta anuvartinām
te tu idānīm janasthāne vasamānā mahābalāḥ |
verses.translation: "You are equally aware of the stationing fourteen thousand braving demons in Janasthaana, who are the followers of the wish of Khara, who are with fiendish exploits, and who are the troublemakers to the sages of Dandaka forest or to the intruders therein, aren't you.

glosses.meaning: attained, targets - marks-demons - or, the possessors, of qualities to pick up quarrels, troublemakers to sages

verses.devanagari:
संगताः परम आयत्ता रामेण सह संयुगे
नाना शस्त्र प्रहरणाः खर प्रमुख राक्षसः |
verses.iast:
saṃgatāḥ parama āyattā rāmeṇa saha saṃyuge
nānā śastra praharaṇāḥ khara pramukha rākśasaḥ |
verses.translation: "But recently those great mighty demons that are the residents of Janasthaana, namely Khara and others, preparing themselves inordinately and wielding diverse weapons and assaulters, for their part had an encounter with Rama in a combat.
notes: This episode is narrated in chapter 33, i.e., the episode of Akampana, but there is a difference in the way of Ravana's narration at this place than the previous one. This is another point to discuss whether Akampana's episode is an original work or an interpolation.

glosses.meaning: verily, in front - that are lead by Khara - others
with diverse, weapons, those weapons that assault - assault and battery
met - had an encounter with Rama.

verses.devanagari:
तेन संजात रोषेण रामेण रण मूर्धनि
अनुक्त्वा परुषम् किंचित् शरैर् व्यापारितम् धनुः |
verses.iast:
tena saṃjāta roṣeṇa rāmeṇa raṇa mūrdhani
anuktvā paruṣam kiñcit śarair vyāpāritam dhanuḥ |
verses.translation: "With rancour tiding in him, and without making any scathing remark in the least, that Rama brought his bow into play with arrows in the van of the combat.

glosses.meaning: well emerged, rancour - rancour tiding in him
scathing remark, at the least, without, saying
bow, with arrows, brought into play.

verses.devanagari:
चतुर्दश सहस्राणि रक्षसाम् उग्र तेजसाम्
निहतानि शरैः दीप्तैः मानुषेण पदातिना |
verses.iast:
caturdaśa sahasrāṇi rakṣasām ugra tejasām
nihatāni śaraiḥ dīptaiḥ mānuṣeṇa padātinā |
verses.translation: "But that foot-soldier, that too, a human, has completely wiped out those fourteen-thousand demons with flaring fieriness with his fierce arrows.

glosses.meaning: with fiery, arrows, completely wiped out.

verses.devanagari:
खरः च निहतः संख्ये दूषणः च निपातितः
हत्वा त्रिशिरसम् च अपि निर्भया दण्डकाः कृताः |
verses.iast:
kharaḥ ca nihataḥ saṃkhye dūṣaṇaḥ ca nipātitaḥ
hatvā triśirasam ca api nirbhayā daṇḍakāḥ kṛtāḥ |
verses.translation: "Khara is hewed down, Duushana is mowed down, and even Trishira is hacked down, thereof that Dandaka forest is rendered free from the fear of demons.

verses.devanagari:
पित्रा निरस्तः क्रुद्धेन स भार्यः क्षीण जीवितः
स हन्ता तस्य सैन्यस्य रामः क्षत्रिय पांसनः |
verses.iast:
pitrā nirastaḥ kruddhena sa bhāryaḥ kṣīṇa jīvitaḥ
sa hantā tasya sainyasya rāmaḥ kṣatriya pāṃsanaḥ |
verses.translation: "He who is put to flight by his infuriated father, and who came to Dandaka forest along with his wife, that ignoble Kshatriya is the slaughterer of that demonic army of mine, as his lifespan is diminished.

glosses.meaning: without, foothold - put to flight - exiled
of that, [demonic-] army, he is the slaughterer of my demonic army.

verses.devanagari:
अशीलः कर्कशः तीक्ष्णो मूर्खो लुब्धो अजित इन्द्रियः
त्यक्त धर्मः तु अधर्म आत्मा भूतानाम् अहिते रतः |
verses.iast:
aśīlaḥ karkaśaḥ tīkṣṇo mūrkho lubdho ajita indriyaḥ
tyakta dharmaḥ tu adharma ātmā bhūtānām ahite rataḥ |
verses.translation: "He is out of character, brutal, firestorm, senseless, selfish, one with his senses unconquered and righteousness discarded, and he is an unrighteous soul just delighting in the disservice of all beings.
notes: kruddhā pitrā nirastaḥ kim?'is he necked out by his angry father?' No. To please Kaikeyi and the boon given to her by his father, Rama is unhoused. sa bhārya= sabhā āryaḥ'in assemblages, venerable one.' Rama is one with high esteem. kśīṇa jīvitaḥ kim?'is his lifespan diminishing? No. He is eternal. kśatriya pāmsana= kśatriyān pāti iti kśatriyaḥ paḥ'because he protects Kshatriya-s he is a noble Kshatriya, and sa ca asau aṃsanaḥ ca, amsana āghāte'enemy destroyer,' destroyer of enemies of Kshatriya-s. karkaśaḥ 'brutal' to enemies, not to adherents, therefore he is: amuurkhaH, alubdhaH: he s not senseless, not selfish. adharma aatmaa kim?No, he is not an unrighteous person. And bhūtānām a hite a rataḥ,'for beings, in disservice, not, delights': he does not delight in the disservice of all created beings.' Thus, he is Supreme Person.

But Rama Tilaka, on the other hand refutes this derivation stating that Ravana is not an out and out devotee of Rama, and these many adhyādhāra-s 'ellipses' need not be brought in to justify mythological import to Ramayana. There is a section of pundits that argue Ramayana precedes 18 purāṇā-sthe 18 mythological treatises, and they refuse to believe that Ravana is NOT a devotee of Rama.

In anyway, the innuendo incorporated in certain verses has given rise to diverse commentaries, but the unity of Ramayana is kept up, either by Shaivaites or Vaishnavaite or other sects of Hindu thinking.

verses.devanagari:
येन वैरम् विना अरण्ये सत्त्वम् आश्रित्य केवलम्
कर्ण नास अपहारेण भगिनी मे विरूपिता |
तस्य भार्याम् जनस्थानात् सीताम् सुर सुत उपमाम्
आनयिष्यामि विक्रम्य सहायः तत्र मे भव |
verses.iast:
yena vairam vinā araṇye sattvam āśritya kevalam
karṇa nāsa apahāreṇa bhaginī me virūpitā |
tasya bhāryām janasthānāt sītām sura suta upamām
ānayiṣyāmi vikramya sahāyaḥ tatra me bhava |
verses.translation: "By whom my sister is disfigured stripping off her nose and ears, that too, without any enmity but just depending upon his own brawn, I would like to inveigle such a man's nymphean wife Seetha holding sway on her in Janasthaana, and in that matter I want you to be my aide in Dandaka forest.

glosses.meaning: ears, nose, due to stripping off
celestials, daughter, similar to - nymph like - nymphean Seetha
to me, as aide, you shall be.

verses.devanagari:
त्वया हि अहम् सहायेन पार्श्वस्थेन महाबल
भ्रातृभिः च सुरान् युद्धे समग्रान् न अभिचिंतये |
तत् सहायो भव त्वम् मे समर्थो हि असि राक्षस
verses.iast:
tvayā hi aham sahāyena pārśvasthena mahābala
bhrātṛbhiḥ ca surān yuddhe samagrān na abhiciṃtaye |
tat sahāyo bhava tvam me samartho hi asi rākṣasa
verses.translation: "Oh, highly powerful Maareecha, with you and with my brothers standing by my side as my associates, I indeed care a damn for all of the gods if they are going to wage a war against me, therefore, oh, demon Maareecha, as you are capable of rendering aid you should indeed become my aide in this venture.

glosses.meaning: towards [them,] I think - I don't care them
you, to me, aide, you become
capable [to render aid,] you are, indeed - in this venture of abducting Seetha.

verses.devanagari:
वीर्ये युद्धे च दर्पे च न हि अस्ति सदृशः तव |
उपायतो महान् शूरो महा माय विशारदः
verses.iast:
vīrye yuddhe ca darpe ca na hi asti sadṛśaḥ tava |
upāyato mahān śūro mahā māya viśāradaḥ
verses.translation: "In valour, war and verve there is none similar to you, you are a topmost stalwart in trickery, and a matchless expert in illusive-tricks.

glosses.meaning: to you, similar one, not, is there, indeed

verses.devanagari:
एतत् अर्थम् अहम् प्राप्तः त्वत् समीपम् निशाचर |
शृणु तत् कर्म साहाय्ये यत् कार्यम् वचनात् मम
verses.iast:
etat artham aham prāptaḥ tvat samīpam niśācara |
śṛṇu tat karma sāhāyye yat kāryam vacanāt mama
verses.translation: "I have come nigh of you only for that reason, oh, nightwalker, and listen to that deed which you have to do in the course of helping me as I detail you.

glosses.meaning: I have, to your, near - nigh, come
by my, word - as I tell you, detail you

verses.devanagari:
सौवर्णः त्वम् मृगो भूत्वा चित्रो रजत बिन्दुभिः |
आश्रमे तस्य रामस्य सीतायाः प्रमुखे चर
verses.iast:
sauvarṇaḥ tvam mṛgo bhūtvā citro rajata bindubhiḥ |
āśrame tasya rāmasya sītāyāḥ pramukhe cara
verses.translation: "On becoming an astounding golden deer with silver dots, you move in front of Seetha in the hermitage of that Rama.

glosses.meaning: Seetha's, before, - in front of, you move.

verses.devanagari:
त्वाम् तु निःसंशयम् सीता दृष्ट्वा तु मृग रूपिणम् |
गृह्यताम् इति भर्तारम् लक्ष्मणम् च अभिधास्यति || |
verses.iast:
tvām tu niḥsaṃśayam sītā dṛṣṭvā tu mṛga rūpiṇam |
gṛhyatām iti bhartāram lakṣmaṇam ca abhidhāsyati || |
verses.translation: "On seeing you in the shape of a deer, Seetha undoubtedly bids her husband forthwith, and even Lakshmana, saying, 'lay hold of it.'

glosses.meaning: thus, to husband, to Lakshmana, also

verses.devanagari:
ततः तयोः अपाये तु शून्ये सीताम् यथा सुखम् |
निराबाधो हरिष्यामि राहुः चन्द्र प्रभाम् इव || |
verses.iast:
tataḥ tayoḥ apāye tu śūnye sītām yathā sukham |
nirābādho hariṣyāmi rāhuḥ candra prabhām iva || |
verses.translation: "Then on the diversion of those two, Rama and Lakshmana, I will comfortably and unimpededly abduct Seetha in that lonely place, as planet Rahu abducts the shine of moon.

glosses.meaning: Rahu the planet, Moon's, shine, as with

verses.devanagari:
ततः पश्चात् सुखम् रामे भार्या आहरण कर्शिते |
विस्रब्धम् प्रहरिष्यामि कृत अर्थेन अन्तर् आत्मना
verses.iast:
tataḥ paścāt sukham rāme bhāryā āharaṇa kar.hśite |
visrabdham prahariṣyāmi kṛta arthena antar ātmanā
verses.translation: "Thereafter Rama will be enervated by the abduction of his wife, and then surely and conveniently I wish to retaliate him if he is going to come up against me, for my inner-soul will be firstly gratified with its volition, namely possessing Seetha." Thus Ravana requested Maareecha.
notes: Maheshvara Tiirtha expresses this in terms of Ravana's devotion to Rama. rāme bhāryā haraṇa karṣite: rāma ibha'Rama, the elephant...' āryā'a venerable one, Seetha...' haraṇa karṣite'by abduction, harmed by...' adhyadhāra: mat śarīramelliptical: 'my body...' tataḥ'thereby, by virtue of my act of abducting...' kṛta arthena antarātmanā upalakśitaḥ san'on my soul-cherished desire becoming fulfilled to get salvation...' pascāt'thereafter...' visrabdham'impeccably...' sukham = moksha, salvation, highest bliss...' prahariṣyāmi: prakarṣeṇa hariṣyāmi'evidently I snatch off that bliss...'

"When I abduct that venerable Seetha, the wife of Elephant like Rama, my body gets harmed like an eclipsed moon, but my soul gets fulfilled as I desire eternal salvation, and I can get it evidently and impeccably at the hand of Rama, owing to the ill-virtue of my abduction of Seetha.

The eclipsing planet Rahu may hide moon temporarily by which the world looses moonshine for a while. If Ravana temporarily hides Seetha, as Rahu hides the moon, Rama, who metaphors with the three worlds, may be in gloom temporarily. But neither Rahu nor Ravana are illuminated or enlightened with the presence of the moonbeams of Seetha, alias Goddess Lakshmi, for they tried to seize that all-illuminating Moon/Seetha by force.

glosses.meaning: fulfilled [gratified in the first instance,] volition, with an inner, soul
conveniently, surely, I wish to retaliate - Rama.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य राम कथाम् श्रुत्वा मारीचस्य महात्मनः |
शुष्कम् समभवत् वक्त्रम् परित्रस्तो बभूव च
verses.iast:
tasya rāma kathām śrutvā mārīcasya mahātmanaḥ |
śuṣkam samabhavat vak.htram paritrasto babhūva ca
verses.translation: On listening the very word of Rama that honest-souled Maareecha's mouth is completely dried up, and he is fully frightened.

glosses.meaning: Rama's, story - very word, mention of Rama

verses.devanagari:
ओष्टौ परिलिहन् शुष्कौ नेत्रैः अनिमिषैः इव |
मृत भूत इव आर्तः तु रावणम् समुत् ईक्षतः
verses.iast:
oṣṭau parilihan śuṣkau netraiḥ animiṣaiḥ iva |
mṛta bhūta iva ārtaḥ tu rāvaṇam samut īkśataḥ
verses.translation: Wetting dried up lips with his tongue he has become goggle-eyed almost like an about-to-die animal, and he agonisingly looked up at Ravana with winkless eyes.
notes: At the very word 'Rama' Maareecha is shuddered. daśānana samudīrita vacanam ākarṇya rāma śabda śravaṇa mātreṇa saṃtrasta hṛdayo mārīcaḥ kṛtānjaliḥ evam uvāca - dk From the time when he was firstly struck by Rama's arrow he retired to hermitage and no demonic activity is undertaken by Maareecha. But now Ravana is instigating, which leads Maareecha to his own end, of which he is perfectly aware.

glosses.meaning: without, wink, as if - he started goggling
lifeless, being, as if - wide-eyed like an about-to-die-animal
well, up, looked] = looked up, with raised and searching eyes.

verses.devanagari:
स रावणम् त्रस्त विषण्ण चेता
महावने राम पराक्रमज्ञः |
कृत अंजलिः तत्त्वम् उवाच वाक्यम्
हितम् च तस्मै हितम् आत्मनः च
verses.iast:
sa rāvaṇam trasta viṣaṇṇa cetā
mahāvane rāma parākramajñaḥ |
kṛta aṃjaliḥ tattvam uvāca vākyam
hitam ca tasmai hitam ātmanaḥ ca
verses.translation: Maareecha's heart sank with scare as he is aware of Rama's valour when he was in the great forest of Tataka, thus suppliantly making palm-fold he started telling about factuality of Rama to Ravana, which is beneficial both to Ravana and to himself, as well, if only Ravana is heedful of it.
